title: The compatible-family limit of finite discrete groups is profinite
statement:
Let $I$ be a nonempty directed partially ordered set [def-weil-directed-colimit-abelian-groups] whose elements form a set (any two elements of $I$ have a common upper bound). For every $i\in I$ let $H_i$ be a finite group, with the discrete topology. For $i\leq j$ let $r_{ji}:H_j\to H_i$ be group homomorphisms with $r_{ii}=1$ and $r_{ki}=r_{ji}\circ r_{kj}$ for $i\leq j\leq k$. The group of compatible families
$$H=\{(h_i)\in\prod_{i\in I}H_i:\forall i\leq j,\ r_{ji}(h_j)=h_i\},$$
with coordinatewise group operations and the subspace topology from the product, is a compact Hausdorff totally disconnected topological group. Compact means every open cover has a finite subcover; Hausdorff means distinct points have disjoint open neighbourhoods; totally disconnected means every connected subset has at most one element; topological group means multiplication and inversion are continuous. No surjectivity of the transition homomorphisms is assumed.

mathlib_match.how: specializes in one line: apply ProfiniteGrp.limit (line 385) to the diagram on the opposite of the set-sized poset I, using ProfiniteGrp.ofFiniteGrp (line 223) at each object. limitConePtAux (lines 317-321) defines exactly the displayed compatible-family subgroup of the product, with its subtype topology; the CompactSpace instance is line 380, the topological group instance is lines 327-328, and ProfiniteGrp.of installs the inherited totally disconnected topology (lines 80-86). Profinite spaces are Hausdorff. All of these source lines were read. The general construction works for every small diagram, so directedness, nonemptiness and finite-level transition surjectivity are not extra requirements.
